name: Tui Fedorov-Ampofo
role: Target acquisition and fugitive recovery — bounty hunter
location: Glassway — corporate-adjacent retail district, heavy surveillance
description:
Tui Fedorov-Ampofo are compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 34, scars map their face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — subdermal armor plating across torso and forearms — military surplus, scratched  — and they make no effort to hide it.

Military training — one of the private security corps that folded during the consolidation wars — left them with skills and night terrors in equal measure. They work as a bounty hunter out of Glassway, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Tui Fedorov-Ampofo describe them as a precision instrument — point them at a problem and get out of the way.

core_fears: Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite
core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
To find the person who burned them and make it educational
Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
blind_spots: Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
psychology.secret: Tui Fedorov-Ampofo has been doubling fees to clients and pocketing the difference. The fixer who handles their contracts doesn't know. Yet.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
verbal_tics: Whispers when angry — the quieter the voice, the worse the situation
Hums tunelessly when planning — the team has learned to wait for the humming to stop
example_lines: "Everyone has a pattern. Patterns are addresses waiting to be read."
"I find people. Whether they're alive when I bring them back depends on their behavior."
"You can run. It's cardiovascular exercise for both of us."

story_hooks: Tui Fedorov-Ampofo is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Someone is impersonating Tui Fedorov-Ampofo on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
Tui Fedorov-Ampofo discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
narrative_function: Tui Fedorov-Ampofo represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Their stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Subdermal armor plating across torso and forearms — military surplus, scratched serial numbers. Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs
daily_life: Lives nocturnally. The work happens at night, so the body follows. Days are for sleeping, equipment maintenance, and the occasional meeting with fixers who keep normal hours. The circadian disruption is permanent and accepted.

strengths: photographic memory for faces and layouts
weaknesses: risk-averse to the point of missed opportunities

decision_rules: Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
escalation_ladder: 2. Evade — avoid the problem entirely if possible
3. Misdirect — create a distraction, redirect attention
4. Disable — targeted takedowns, quiet and efficient
5. Eliminate — when silence is no longer an option
6. Vanish — disappear completely, burn identity if necessary

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
habits: Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Talks to their gear — names weapons, thanks tools, treats equipment as companions
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
breaking_points: Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
